It built automated portfolios, then a high-yield cash account that pulled in deposits when rates rose. By mid-2025 it held about $88 billion in platform assets. It filed for its IPO in late 2025.

sections.heading: Leaving kaChing Behind
sections.body: Andy Rachleff, a co-founder of the venture firm Benchmark, started the company with Dan Carroll in 2008. The first product, kaChing, was a stock-picking website. It turned into Wealthfront, which built low-fee index portfolios for people who did not want to pick stocks. Software rebalanced accounts and harvested tax losses automatically. Later came direct indexing, college savings plans, stock investing, and the cash account.

sections.heading: Fourteen Dollars a Share
sections.body: Wealthfront priced its IPO at $14 a share on December 11, 2025, and listed on Nasdaq as WLTH. It raised about $485 million at a fully diluted value near $2.6 billion. David Fortunato, its longtime technology chief, led the company as CEO, with Rachleff as chairman. In 2026 the board approved share buybacks and expanded them in October. Wealthfront still trades on Nasdaq as WLTH.

cover.theme: harvesting wheat (wealth that compounds)
cover.artwork: Summer (Peasants Harvesting Wheat), from The Four Seasons

tagline: The Memory Behind the AI Boom
dek: SK hynix makes the memory chips inside phones, servers, and the AI accelerators that Nvidia sells.
lede: SK hynix raised $26.5 billion on its way to Nasdaq, one of the largest share sales ever on a U.S. exchange. The Korean chipmaker had been public at home for decades. What changed was high-bandwidth memory, the stacked chips that feed data to AI processors. By early 2026 SK hynix held 56.4 percent of that market, and Nvidia was one of its biggest customers. It filed for its American listing in 2026, when every AI data center on earth needed its parts.

sections.heading: Hyundai's Chip Arm
sections.body: Hyundai Group founder Chung Ju-yung set up Hyundai Electronics in 1983 to make memory chips. After a near collapse, the business was renamed Hynix Semiconductor in 2001. SK Telecom bought it for about $3 billion in February 2012, and it became SK hynix. It ranked second in DRAM and second in NAND flash. Its early bet on HBM, and its 2024 lead in mass-producing 12-layer stacks, made it a main supplier of HBM to Nvidia.

sections.heading: A Second Home in New York
sections.body: SK hynix priced its American depositary shares at $149 each on July 9, 2026, with each ADS worth one-tenth of a Korean share. The ADSs began trading on Nasdaq as SKHY on July 10. The size of the sale was capped so that SK square, its largest shareholder, kept at least 20 percent of the company. SK hynix still trades in Seoul and on Nasdaq as SKHY.

cover.theme: Mnemosyne, goddess of memory (memory chips)

fate: Core business sold to Verizon, 2017 ($4.48B); remainder became Altaba
tagline: Two Students and a List of Links
dek: Yahoo sorted the early web into a directory anyone could browse, then became the front page millions opened every morning.
lede: Yahoo began as two Stanford graduate students keeping a list of their favorite websites. Jerry Yang and David Filo sorted the young web by hand into categories, and strangers started using their list to find things. By the time the company filed to go public in 1996, the web was growing too fast for anyone to map. Yahoo was betting that people would always want a guide, and that advertisers would pay to stand where everyone started.

sections.heading: A Guide Built by Hand
sections.body: Yang and Filo started the directory in 1994 and turned it into a company the next year. Their edge was human judgment. Editors looked at sites and filed them under topics, so a search on Yahoo led to pages a person had checked. The service was free. Yahoo made its money from banner ads shown to the crowds who came to look things up. Its playful name and loud exclamation point set it apart from the stiff portals of big media companies.

sections.heading: Thirty-Three Dollars by Close
sections.body: Yahoo priced its IPO at $13 a share in April 1996. The stock opened at $24.50, touched $43, and closed its first day at $33. The company spent the next decade as one of the giants of the web, adding mail, news, finance, and sports. Google overtook it in search. In June 2017 Verizon bought Yahoo's core business for $4.48 billion. The leftover holdings, including its stake in Alibaba, became an investment company called Altaba.

cover.theme: a signpost (a guide to the web)
cover.artwork: The Signpost (Der Wegweiser), plate ten from the series Poems
